qa_pairs.query: How does Zeekr justify seeking a separate listing from Geely Auto, and what specific types of independence does it say it needs?

qa_pairs.query: What sequence of corporate structuring steps did Zeekr take in March and April 2021 across the Cayman Islands, British Virgin Islands, and Hong Kong?
qa_pairs.ground_truth_answer: In March 2021, Zeekr incorporated ZEEKR Intelligent Technology as an exempted company with limited liability under Cayman Islands law to act as its holding company; in April 2021, it incorporated ZEEKR Innovation as a wholly-owned subsidiary of ZEEKR Intelligent Technology under British Virgin Islands law, and in the same period incorporated ZEEKR Technology (a wholly-owned subsidiary of ZEEKR Innovation) under Hong Kong law.

qa_pairs.query: Does Zeekr’s timeline indicate that vehicle deliveries began before or after it had consolidated full ownership of key operating entities, and what events and dates support that conclusion?
qa_pairs.ground_truth_answer: Deliveries began before Zeekr had consolidated full ownership of several key entities: it launched its first BEV model ZEEKR 001 in April 2021 and started delivery from October 2021, while later ownership steps include acquiring 100% equity interest in ZEEKR Shanghai in August 2021, acquiring 51% equity interest in Ningbo Viridi in October 2021, and acquiring 100% equity interest in CEVT in February 2022.

qa_pairs.query: What does the 2021–2023 mix of Zeekr’s cost of revenues suggest about whether rising vehicle sales costs were the main driver of total cost growth?
qa_pairs.ground_truth_answer: Rising vehicle sales costs appear to be the main driver of total cost of revenues growth because the vehicle sales line increases sharply from RMB (1,515,797) in 2021 to RMB (18,748,155) in 2022 and RMB (28,831,552) in 2023, while its share of total cost of revenues also rises from 27.6% (2021) to 63.7% (2022) and 64.3% (2023). Over the same period, total cost of revenues grows from RMB (5,489,349) to RMB (29,427,398) to RMB (44,822,088), and other categories (like batteries/components) do not increase as much in share (38.9% in 2021 down to 31.4% in 2022 and 30.8% in 2023).

qa_pairs.query: Does Zeekr’s R&D spending shift from outsourcing toward internal employee compensation between 2021 and 2023, and what evidence supports that?
qa_pairs.ground_truth_answer: Yes, the mix shifts toward internal employee compensation: outsourcing R&D expenses fall from 69.3% of total R&D in 2021 to 51.3% in 2022 and 42.9% in 2023, while employee compensation rises from 22.9% (2021) to 36.5% (2022) and 40.0% (2023). In absolute terms, outsourcing grows from RMB (2,192,512) in 2021 to RMB (3,591,570) in 2023, but compensation grows more sharply from RMB (722,438) to RMB (3,349,231), indicating a larger internalization of R&D cost structure.

qa_pairs.query: Is it reasonable to claim that Zeekr’s cost of revenues became more concentrated in a single category by 2023 compared with 2021, and why?
qa_pairs.ground_truth_answer: Yes, concentration increases by 2023 because vehicle sales becomes the dominant component: in 2021, the largest category (sales of batteries and other components) is 38.9% and vehicle sales is only 27.6%, whereas by 2023 vehicle sales alone accounts for 64.3% of total cost of revenues (RMB (28,831,552) out of total RMB (44,822,088)). Meanwhile, the other two categories in 2023 are much smaller shares—sales of batteries and other components at 30.8% and R&D service/other services at 4.9%—showing a more single-category-heavy mix than in 2021 (27.6%, 38.9%, and 33.5%).
